title: P142's suites pass on every CI runner: Windows paths across drives, spaced and linked temp roots
desiredOutcome: The release-tier CI run (ci.yml -f tier=release) is green on the commit that carries P142 and these fixes, every selftests leg included (linux stress, windows plain and cp1252)

findings.issue: No case pins the quoting on a plain run. kt5/kt7/kt9/kt9b/kt6b/kt8 only see a path that needs quoting when the sweep's TMPDIR holds a space (--spaced leg) or on Windows; on a plain POSIX run every fixture path is shell-safe, so `_shell_word` returning `text` unquoted would leave the task's own gate command (`sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_status.py`, 407 cases, run by me: exit 0) green. The executor's own mutation proof is red only under --spaced.
findings.resolution: Add one deterministic case that does not depend on the temp root: call `M._kept_tree_remedy('P2.1 set aside 1', <path with a space, a single quote and a backslash>, None)` and assert `_posix_words(remedy)` equals ['git','worktree','remove','--force', path] and that the saveFirst entries read back to the same one-word path through `_posix_words`. Then the fix is red on any leg, not only the spaced one.

findings.issue: GIT_PATH_BASE_EXEMPT reason rows for drive-phase.py tree_changed and _changed_between still say the paths are 'handed back as literal pathspecs to git'. This diff removes exactly that for _changed_between (and _unheld) and tree_changed never did it, so the table now states the opposite of the code. The lint passes (it reads the rows' presence, not their prose), so nothing will catch it. The executor reported it as LEFT (b), the file being outside the task's files.
findings.resolution: Reword both rows to say the listings are narrowed in Python by _literal_matches, in a follow-up task that owns tools/lints/_deps.py.

findings.issue: ar22's pathspec-matching branch in _command_line_git (the specs / startswith(tag) handling) is never reached by the fixed product, since _changed_between and _unheld now pass no pathspec. It only bites if someone reintroduces :(literal) arguments. That is the intended guard, but a reader cannot tell from the case that the branch is dormant, and nothing asserts that no argv in `seen` carries a pathspec. `len(seen)` is recorded in `answered` but never compared.
findings.resolution: Either assert that no recorded argv holds a ':(literal)' element (turning the dormant branch into a live pin that a reintroduction trips under the posix leg as well), or drop the unused `seen` count from `answered`.

review.outcome: [findings: 3 - 0 high, 0 med, 3 low; 0 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: prove-gates' selftest reads its fixture tree when the fixture and the repository sit on different Windows drives
tasks.description: CI run 40715565769 (release tier, f06f113f), windows plain 3 and cp1252 3: tools/prove-gates.py --selftest raised 'ValueError: path is on mount C:, start on mount D:' at _cases line 3153 'coverage(script_dir=_fx)' -> gate_names -> _derived_gates line 2011 (an os.path.relpath of a fixture dir under the temp root on C: against the repo on D:); every case after it did not run (8/9). Logs: <scratchpad>/ci142/122912182409.log. Make the derivation never relpath across drives (spell the fixture's paths relative to its own root, or compare by realpath without relpath), keep the cases' meaning, and add a case that fails on a POSIX host by simulating the cross-drive answer (inject the relpath, or a fixture outside the repo root) so the class is caught off Windows. Check every other relpath in prove-gates.py for the same shape.

outcome.technical: tools/prove-gates.py: _gate_sources() now returns (rel, path, tree), rel spelled against the root the walk started from: '<_GATE_ROOTS entry>/' + relpath(path, root) for the repo roots, relpath(path, script_dir) for a fixture. A walked file always shares its root's drive, so no relpath crosses drives. _derived_gates() reads that rel instead of os.path.relpath(path, repo_root) (the CI line 2011 crash). not_a_gate_problems() unpacks the triple. Over the live tree the derivation is byte-identical: HEAD's and the new module's _derived_gates(repo=R), guard_files(repo=R) and lint_homes(repo=R) compared equal (72 == 72 entries, True/True/True, exit 0). New case c1g: the same unproven-lint fixture, with os.path.relpath swapped for a stub that raises Windows' ValueError when exactly one side is under the fixture (simulated other drive) and delegates otherwise; it asserts the stub is armed (the patched name is the stub and it refuses the fixture-vs-REPO pair) and that coverage(script_dir=fixture) == ['probe_unproven_violations']; restored in finally. The arming probe calls the stub by name, because spelling os.path.relpath(<mkdtemp path>, REPO) tripped _suite.unsafe_relpath_violations() (seen: it reported prove-gates.py line 3196; now []). Every other drive-crossing call in the file checked: grep -n 'relpath|commonpath|relative_to|commonprefix' tools/prove-gates.py -> line 864/866 and 1555 are row payload strings/lint names, not calls; 2001 is the new within-root call; 3182-3205 the case's stub; 3675 _text_homes relpath(path, root) with path walked under os.path.join(root, top), same drive, left. Gates: sweep-selftests.py tools/prove-gates.py tests/test__refs.py exit 0 (61 + 292 cases ok); prove-gates --selftest exit 0, 61/61; sweep tools/_suite.py exit 0 (34 cases); ruff exit 0; vermin exit 0; prose_number_claims and house_style_violations report nothing for prove-gates.py. No full prove-gates run, as instructed. Dependants: drive-phase.py lint_probe - main()'s output and exit codes untouched (only _gate_sources/_derived_gates internals and one selftest case changed), still correct; tests/test__refs.py tb1 - the only .py basename literal added is _output.py, which exists, tb1 green in the sweep above; .github/sweep-costs.json, guard-bash-writes.py, tests/_harness.py, test__deps.py, test__gate_feed.py, test_drive_phase.py, test_guard_bash_writes.py, affected.py name the file's path, which did not move - still correct; names used elsewhere (_git, selector_text, _call_name, _under) unchanged, _under is only newly called by c1g; GUARD_FILES/lint_homes unchanged per the equality check above.
outcome.descriptive: prove-gates' lint derivation no longer builds a relative path across drives, so its selftest survives a Windows runner whose temp directory is on another drive, and a POSIX case simulates that drive split.

verifiedBy: c1g: the unproven-lint fixture is derived the same when os.path.relpath raises Windows' cross-drive ValueError for any pair with one side inside the fixture, with the injection shown armed first

redFirst.basis: Mode regression, expectRedFirst false, and the case and the fix live in the one file tools/prove-gates.py, so the helper's tree (HEAD plus the declared test files copied over it) carries the fix and cannot separate the two; no helper run was made. Reds watched by hand, for the record: (1) case c1g written BEFORE the fix, run in my tree on HEAD's derivation: `python3 tools/prove-gates.py --selftest` exit 1, 'FAIL c1g ... (injection armed: True; derived "raised ValueError: path is on mount 'C:', start on mount 'D:'")', 'SELFTEST FAILED: 60/61 cases passed'. (2) After the fix, in a throwaway `git archive HEAD` export under the scratchpad with the new file copied in and ONLY _derived_gates mutated back to os.path.relpath(path, repo_root): exit 1, the same FAIL c1g line and 60/61; export deleted. Fixed tree: exit 0, 'ALL PASS: 61/61 cases passed'.

tasks.title: Status's kept-tree remover rows hold under a spaced, symlinked temp root and on Windows
tasks.description: CI run 40715565769 (release tier, f06f113f): tests/test_audit_status.py kt5, kt6b, kt7, kt8, kt9, kt9b fail (401/407) on linux stress 3 (cp1252 + spaced, symlinked TMPDIR: '/tmp/sw-x/via/s p/...' where via is a link to real) and on windows plain 3 and cp1252 3. Example kt5: the aside row prints "git worktree remove --force '/tmp/sw-xz1zqqsk/via/s p/audit-status-kt-yvs53rj2/aside-tree'" (shlex-quoted because of the space) while the case expects the bare path; kt6b: the row names the 'real/' spelling while the fixture holds the 'via/' one, and running the row as written did not take the tree down (None). These cases came in with 152b7253 (kept-tree advice). Logs: <scratchpad>/ci142/122912183449.log (linux), <scratchpad>/ci142/122912182409.log (windows). Reproduce locally with 'python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --spaced tests/test_audit_status.py' (and --encoding cp1252). Decide per case whether the PRODUCT is wrong (a printed command must run as written in the user's shell - on Windows too, where POSIX single quotes do not quote in cmd; say which shells the printed command targets and quote for them) or the CASE compares a spelling it should normalise (realpath both sides). Fix the product where it is wrong; never weaken a case to the observed output. The release-tier CI must be green on these legs.

outcome.technical: Diagnosis. The CI rows quote a kept tree's path with shlex.quote (POSIX sh) because the path holds a space (linux stress, spaced TMPDIR) or backslashes (Windows). The cases looked for the bare path, so kt5/kt7/kt9/kt9b compared a spelling a shell would split in two. kt6b's guard `named in rows[0]` failed on the quoting, so it ran nothing (ran=None). kt8's save filter `-C <bare tree> ` matched nothing (saves=[]). The brief reads kt6b as a real/ vs via/ mismatch, which does not match the log: the case realpaths its base, and the linux log's row and fixture both carry real/ (122912183449.log:572), so the miss was the quoting. The product is right for the shell it targets. Every command this plugin prints or runs is quoted with shlex.quote for a POSIX shell, and _proc_group.locate_sh resolves that shell on Windows too (Git for Windows' sh; it never falls back to cmd.exe). The plugin has no cmd.exe or PowerShell quoting helper to match, and I wrote no second copy of a helper. Product change: _shell_word's docstring (plugins/audit/scripts/status/audit-status.py:2080) now says which shell the rows target (sh/bash, Git for Windows' sh on Windows, not cmd.exe or PowerShell) and that git's own sh reads the inner submodule-foreach command. No executable byte changed. Case changes (tests/test_audit_status.py): new helpers _posix_words (shlex.split, None on an unbalanced quote), _remedy_after (the command after a row's ` <path> - `), _run_as_written (runs the printed text under _proc_group.shell_invocation, the plugin's own resolved POSIX shell, so Windows uses git's sh and not a bare `sh` on PATH; None reads as failure) and _listed_worktrees/_one_spelling (realpath plus normcase, because git lists forward slashes on Windows). kt5, kt9 and kt9b now assert the words a POSIX shell reads equal ['git','worktree','remove',('--force',) <path>]. kt7 asserts exactly 2 save lines, the update-ref pin once, and one foreach push whose inner command reads the tree as one word. kt6b now runs the row's printed text as written instead of rebuilding argv by split(' '). It also checks that git listed the tree BEFORE the remove, in the spelling the after-check reads, so 'lists it no more' is a watched change and cannot pass because the spellings never matched. kt8 picks its saves by the -C word a shell reads and runs them under the same resolved shell. No assertion was loosened to the observed output: each now asserts what a shell reads, and the mutation runs show it red when the path is not one word. Runs (all exit 0, '1/1 files ok, 407 cases'): `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_status.py`, the same with `--spaced`, and with `--encoding cp1252`. Also a direct run under TMPDIR='<scratch>/via/s p', via being a link to real: every kt case PASS. In that run sl1-sl3 FAIL (404/407) only because the direct run keeps the session's CLAUDE_* variables, which `_cli` drops and `_in_project` does not. They pass under the sweep, and I did not touch them. ruff check on both files: exit 0. vermin -t=3.8-: exit 0. _output_lints.prose_number_claims() and house_style_violations(): 0 findings. NOT VERIFIED: Windows. I could not run the Windows legs. kt6b and kt8 now really run git worktree remove --force, update-ref and a submodule-foreach push to a C:\ path under git's sh there; until now they never ran on Windows (ran=None, saves=[]). The owner can check with `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_audit_status.py` on Windows; expected '1/1 files ok, 407 cases'. Dependants: audit-status.py renders byte-identical output, so /audit:status, /audit:worktree, drive-phase.py's kept-tree advice (P142.47/.49 aside keys, --force only for an aside key; kt9c still pins ASIDE_KEY), tests/test_drive_phase.py, tests/test_run_test_gate.py, tools/verify.sh, CONTRIBUTING.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md, docs/examples/azure-pipelines.yml, docs/research/pipeline-cost-results.md and docs/demo-large.html stay correct: no behaviour or name changed. The test file's dependants stay correct as well. .github/sweep-costs.json: same cases, same spawn count; kt6b/kt8 now run through the resolved shell instead of a direct git/sh spawn, so the per-file cost is materially unchanged. tools/affected.py maps by path, unchanged. _live_copy.py and tests/test__status_facts.py are basename mentions; _cases, _fixture and _selftest are untouched.
outcome.descriptive: The kept-tree cases now judge a printed remover by the words a POSIX shell reads and run it as written, so they hold under a spaced or symlinked temp root and on Windows; the product's POSIX quoting was already right, and its target shell is now stated in the code.

verifiedBy: kt5/kt7/kt9/kt9b assert the printed remover and save commands read, in a POSIX shell, as the exact word list with the tree path as one word (red when the path is printed unquoted under a spaced root)
kt6b runs the row's remover text as written under the plugin's resolved POSIX shell and checks git listed the tree before and not after, in one realpath+normcase spelling
kt8 selects the save commands by the -C word a shell reads and runs them as written under the same shell

redFirst.basis: Regression task, expectRedFirst false, and the fix is in the CASES: audit-status.py's executable bytes are unchanged (only _shell_word's docstring grew), so HEAD's code under the new cases is green by design and the helper has no red to find. The reproduction was watched on HEAD before any edit: `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --spaced tests/test_audit_status.py` -> FAIL kt5, kt7, kt9, kt9b, kt6b, kt8, 'SELFTEST FAILED: 401/407 cases passed', 0/1 files ok. That the corrected cases can fail was proven in a throwaway git-archive export (not the shared tree): _shell_word mutated to `return text` (unquoted) -> under --spaced, kt5, kt7, kt9, kt9b, kt6b, kt8 FAIL, 401/407, exit 1. Allow direction: _shell_word mutated to always single-quote (another valid POSIX spelling) -> plain and --spaced both exit 0, 407 cases. So the cases pin what a POSIX shell reads, not one spelling.
redFirst.at: 2026-10-28 (reproduction and mutation runs made by hand in this session; the helper was not run)

tasks.title: The drive's redo-recut cases hold on Windows: staged deletions, skip-worktree files and non-UTF-8 path bytes
tasks.description: CI run 40715565769 (release tier, f06f113f), windows plain 1: tests/test_drive_phase.py ar20, ar20b, ar21, ar22 fail (649/653); windows cp1252 1: the ar block did not finish within 447 s (DID NOT REPORT). Linux and macOS pass. ar20: a staged deletion of a file still on disk - the redo is refused naming src/f3.txt 'staged as neither its base nor the work holds it', where the case expects a refusal by name with the index as it was (read the exact expectation); ar20b: a staged edit whose file was put back - the drive went on to an undeclared-change decision instead of refusing; ar21: a skip-worktree file absent from disk; ar22: a path in non-UTF-8 bytes - the pathspec handed to git is b':(literal)caf\xed\xb3\xa9.txt' (surrogateescape re-encoded as UTF-8 surrogates) where the listing returned 'caf\udce9.txt' - on Windows the filesystem encoding differs (os.fsencode is not surrogateescape there). Logs: <scratchpad>/ci142/122912182618.log; the cp1252 1 timeout: gh run view 40715565769 --job 122912182623 --log-failed. For each: decide whether the PRODUCT is wrong on Windows (git index reads, CRLF/autocrlf turning a put-back file into a modification, filesystem encoding of path bytes) or whether a case asserts a property Windows cannot hold (then the case says so by platform, with the reason, never silently skipped). Fix the product where it is wrong. Also say why the ar block takes > 447 s on cp1252 1 and whether its recorded cost in .github/sweep-costs.json needs re-recording (that file is not in scope - report it).

tasks.title: The sweep's per-file cost table is re-recorded from the windows release-tier log, so a staged block's timeout fits the windows runner
tasks.description: CI run 40715565769 (release tier, f06f113f), windows cp1252 1: tests/test_drive_phase.py's ar block did not finish within 447 s (DID NOT REPORT). A block's timeout is derived from the file's recorded cost in .github/sweep-costs.json (test_drive_phase.py: 1346.4 slot-seconds), while that run reported 4913.5 s for the file on cp1252 and 4375.4 s on plain - about 3.2-3.6x the record. Re-record the table from the windows plain legs of that run (gh run view 40715565769 --job <id> --log for each windows plain shard, saved locally) with 'python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log LOG --platform win32 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json', per the file's own 'about' text, merging all shards so every file has a figure; check that '--shard I/N' still prints a balanced split and that sweep-selftests' own --selftest and gate-parity.py pass on the new table. If one log cannot carry every file, say which files keep their old figure and why. Report the before/after figure for test_drive_phase.py and the derived ar-block timeout. This does not settle P142-R9 (true per-block costs, P143.6); say so in the outcome.
